title: Improving Semantic Coverage in AI Test & Evaluation through Generative Augmentation
venue: Hashemi, Connor, et al. "Improving semantic coverage in AI test and evaluation through generative augmentation." Society of Photo-Optical Instrumentation Engineers (SPIE) Conference Series. Vol. 14046. 2026

problem.summary: In test and evaluation (T&E) of AI models, evaluators typically have access only to a held-out test dataset and no knowledge of the training data or its semantic composition.
statements: In test and evaluation (T&E) of AI models, evaluators typically have access only to a held-out test dataset and no knowledge of the training data or its semantic composition.
If critical input conditions-such as time-of-day, weather, or scene location-are underrepresented in this test dataset, T&E results can be misleadingly due to this semantic coverage gap.
We propose a three-stage generative AI pipeline to detect and fill such semantic gaps without requiring ground-truth labels of these semantics.

background.summary: Existing data augmentations are poorly suited for generating realistic, high-level semantic variations that preserve task-relevant content.

evidence.quote: Existing data augmentations are poorly suited for generating realistic, high-level semantic variations that preserve task-relevant content.

By filling these gaps with targeted synthetic augmentations on already existing imagery in the dataset, our method significantly improves the robustness of T&E for image classification and object detection models.
